newsitem.title: USA: American Media 1996 revs seen rising - report.
newsitem.headline: American Media 1996 revs seen rising - report.

text.p: American Media Operations Inc, which owns the supermarket tabloid that published a story alleging a presidential campaign adviser had a relationship with a call girl, is expected to report stronger revenues this year, weekly financial tabloid Barron's reported.

Citing John Rogers, who heads the Ariel Growth fund and owns stock in the company, the tabloid said the cost of newsprint was going down and conventional advertisers were returning to the pages of The Star after it reported on Dick Morris allegedly sleeping with a call girl.
Rogers told Barron's American Media would likely reduce its debt and interest costs, bringing earnings to $0.25 a share this year with about $0.50 in non-cash charges.
He said he eventually saw a 50-percent appreciation.
Morris resigned from President Clinton's re-election campaign on Thursday after the tabloid said he had a year-long affair with a prostitute and had confided White House secrets to her.
